records.title: Cluster Expansion
author: Roman Kotecky
records.version_date: Encyclopedia of Mathematical Physics article (2006); PDF as served 2026-09-24
records.section: Section 2 abstract polymer models: Dobrushin condition (24) and the Theorem (cluster expansion) (i)-(ii); Section 3.2 correlations: alpha-modified partition function (42)-(48) and the boundary-decay estimate (49)
records.provenance: institutional page (author-hosted PDF); text extracted locally with pdftotext after WebFetch returned binary
records.claim: For an abstract hard-core polymer gas with weights in a polydisc satisfying the Dobrushin condition R(v) <= r(v) prod_{v' in N(v)} (1-r(v')), log Z_W is an absolutely convergent series with sum over clusters containing v bounded by -log(1-r(v)); local expectations are linear terms of an alpha-modified cluster expansion, and |<Psi> - <Psi>_Lambda| <= |S| K^{-dist(S,Lambda^c)} when sum_{A ni x}|w(A)| K^{|Lambda(A)|} <= 1.
records.relevance: Exact template for memo section 2.5: the creation-product vector psi(s) gives a hard-core polymer gas of pairs (F,F') with site-disjoint compatibility; the boundary-decay estimate (49) is the mechanism of the proposed BB1 forward route.
records.unresolved: Classical-statistical-mechanics setting; the quantum polymer representation of <psi(sbar),psi(s)> and its weights must be derived for the AM2 creation algebra; no constant transfers.

records.title: Lieb-Robinson Bounds and the Exponential Clustering Theorem
author: Bruno Nachtergaele
Robert Sims
records.section: Section 2: norm (1) with |X| N^{2|X|} e^{lambda D(X)} weights; Theorem 1 (Lieb-Robinson bound, eqs. (4)-(7)); Theorem 2 (exponential clustering, eqs. (10)-(14)) with c(A,B) and mu = gamma lambda/(4||Phi||_lambda + gamma)
records.provenance: arXiv author preprint with journal reference; text extracted locally with pdftotext (the WebFetch summary was a paraphrase and was not used)
records.claim: A spectral gap gamma implies |<Omega,A tau_{ib}(B) Omega>| <= c(A,B) exp(-mu d (1 + gamma^2 b^2/(4 mu^2 d^2))) for 0 <= gamma b <= 2 mu d, with mu = gamma lambda/(4||Phi||_lambda + gamma) and c(A,B) = ||A|| ||B|| (1 + 2|Y|/pi + (pi mu d)^{-1/2}); trivial bound e^{-gamma b} for large b; assumes a uniform bound N on single-site dimensions.
records.relevance: Route B of memo section 2.6 (static susceptibility by imaginary-time clustering); with the F-norm substitution C_F||Phi||_{F_lambda} = 224*2268 e^{2 lambda}|tau| the preview rate at the cap is mu_B ~ 0.841 at lambda ~ 1.34.
records.unresolved: Finite-dimensional sites assumed (the norm carries N^{2|X|}); the adaptation to unbounded commuting onsite Casimir terms in the interaction picture is unproved here.

records.claim: For gapped quantum spin systems with local interactions, a transformation between gapped eigenvectors and their perturbations that is local with exponential (not sub-exponential) decay in the distance to the perturbation, improving spectral-flow locality bounds for models with a unique bulk ground state or topological order.
records.relevance: Candidate tool to sharpen route B (boundary influence through the uniform AM2 gap along the interpolation H(theta)).
records.unresolved: Body not read; hypotheses (bounded site spaces, interaction class) unchecked against unbounded Casimir onsite terms; constants not evaluated.

records.title: Uniqueness of the Ground State in Weak Perturbations of Non-Interacting Gapped Quantum Lattice Systems

records.section: Search-result summary of the abstract (publisher page behind a login gate, as recorded in Round32)
records.claim: In finite volume the dependence of the ground state of a weak perturbation of a non-interacting gapped system on the boundary condition decays exponentially with the distance to the boundary, implying uniqueness of the infinite-volume ground state.
records.relevance: The external theorem closest to the Round33 direction: its boundary-decay part is the BB1 target for the named constructions; its uniqueness part is the strong form of obligation O1 (BC2).
records.unresolved: Text not read; constants existential; onsite dimension and boundedness hypotheses unchecked; no premise.
